happens with the weather if it's stable your payouts are low if hurricanes hit unexpectedly payouts are high implied volatility on the other hand is the forecast what people think will happen in the future if they expect hurricanes they'll pay more for insurance even if the storm never comes in options trading realized volatility is how much the ndx NASDAQ 100 actually moves implied volatility IV is how much the options Market expects ndx to move in the future now how does an options seller make money in a slow down Trend imagine a casino owner he makes money when gamblers overestimate their ch chances of winning now let's say an options seller writes a contract expecting ndx to have big swings High IV but the market moves down slowly at a constant Pace because the market is moving in a predictable controlled way low realized volatility the options seller profits why because options were priced as if the market would swing wildly High implied volatility but that didn't happen so as long as the market continues in a steady downtrend the seller keeps pocketing the premiums but here's where the game changes imagine you're riding a bike downhill at a steady Pace low realized volatility shifts the market moves more than expected option sellers who are making easy money now panic and adjust their positions causing even more volatility so why does this happen options pricing is based on future expectations IV when the market is predictable realized volatility stays low and sellers profit when the market surprises everyone with a big move or reversal realized volatility spikes and option sellers are suddenly in trouble to sum it all up if the market trends steadily option sellers win because realized volatility stays lower than implied volatility but if a sudden
